card: Replaces hard-coded numeric RPC error codes across functional tests and unit tests with named `RPCErrorCode` constants. This solves test readability and maintainability issues where developers must look up error code numbers to understand expected failure conditions. The PR touches 126 test files, primarily driven by scripted diffs, with no changes to node behavior or dependencies.
evidence: Author states: 'When a test expects an RPC error by number, readers have to look up the code to tell which failure it covers.' (PR description)
Author notes the change was split out while reviewing #36976 (PR description)
problem: Tests asserting on expected RPC errors use raw numeric codes like `-8` or `-25`. Developers reading or reviewing test failures must manually look up what error condition a numeric code represents.

risk.why: Touches only tests and test framework definitions without altering production code.

scope_notes: Large mechanical change across 126 files generated largely by scripted-diffs (commit `f3c2f5240f` and `dfca8948a9`). A verification script using sed is provided in the description to confirm numeric values were not altered.
summary: Replaces hard-coded numeric RPC error codes across the test suite with named constants. It exposes the C++ `RPCErrorCode` enum values to the Python test framework in `test_framework/rpc_error_codes.py`, updates assertions in functional tests to use named error codes, and updates C++ RPC unit tests and test client error definitions accordingly.
